## 5. Findings (prioritized; all pinned by tests; none fixed because the code is outside owned paths)

| id | sev | what | where | pinned by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SEC-F5** | **HIGH** | The assembler's forbidden-call scan is a regex for `file(`; a comment between the name and the paren (`${file/**/("/proc/self/environ")}`, `# c` / `// c` + newline) passes and **real OpenTofu 1.12.5 evaluates it** (proved: read `versions.tf.json` back through the plan). Works for `file`, `templatefile`, `fileexists`, nested in `try()`, inside `%{ if }`. `path . cwd` and `path/**/.cwd` leak the runner's absolute work dir the same way. Impact: if any manifest/repo-derived string reaches a fragment unescaped, arbitrary file read on the runner/worker host (`/proc/self/environ` of the tofu child holds the brokered cloud creds; `/proc/<pid>/environ` of the worker holds control-plane secrets). Drivers (not yet merged) are meant to escape `${`; this is the second wall and it is bypassable. | `src/lib/tofu/workspace.ts:139-140` (`FORBIDDEN_CALL`, `FORBIDDEN_REF`), `scanExpressions` :154 | `tofu-workspace-injection.test.ts` "SEC-F5 (HIGH)" and "SEC-F5 (LOW part)" (`it.fails`, real tofu). Suggested fix: do not regex; tokenize/strip HCL comments+whitespace, or better refuse any `${`/`%{` in leaf strings unless produced by the driver's own reference helper (allowlist), and allowlist functions. |
| SEC-F4 | MED | `nonsensitive()` not forbidden: a fragment can unmask a value tofu marked sensitive (e.g. from `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version`), so it reaches `planView` / the model. Mechanism shown with `sensitive()` -> `nonsensitive()` in real tofu. | `workspace.ts:139` | `it.fails` in `tofu-workspace-injection.test.ts` (known gaps) |
| SEC-F8 | MED | Policy: `agent_high_risk_requires_approval` keys on `context.origin` only. An `integration` principal with `origin:"human"` runs `infrastructure.apply` etc. unattended in dev; a `navigator` principal with `origin:"human"` in **production at autonomy 5**. Safe only if the broker labels origin from the authenticated principal (pending hook for WS-CAP). | `policy/rego/approval.rego:137` (+ rebuild `policy/dist/policy.wasm`) | two `it.fails` in `policy-invariants.test.ts` (P7) |
| SEC-F9 | MED (runtime) | Node 24.x (V8 13.6, incl. this machine's 24.19.0) has a `JSON.parse` bug (nodejs/node#60606, V8 >= 12.8.367; Node 22/V8 12.4 unaffected): after a parse of an object with a key ending in a backslash, later parses can return a WRONG single-character key (`{"a":1}` -> `{"\\":1}`). Reproduced independently in plain node (6% of random flat objects). Zenith parses untrusted JSON everywhere and digests the PARSED value. CI and the Dockerfile pin Node 22, but `package.json engines.node` is `>=22.16` (admits 24/26). | `package.json:6`; runtime | `runtime-sanity.test.ts` (reports the state; `it.fails` for the engines range); `skipIfJsonParseBroken` skips 2 digest tests loudly on affected runtimes (UNVERIFIED on Node 22.16 here: only Node 24 is installed) |

Redirects/weakens the API traffic that carries brokered creds. Not reachable from a manifest TODAY (`providerConfig` is only consumed by `assembleWorkspace`; manifest V2 `providerConfig` per ADR-0003 would feed it). | `workspace.ts` `providersFile` ~:317, `CREDENTIAL_KEY` :142 | `it.fails` |

Audit redaction is key-name based only; blob inputs leak. Also pinned: audit `error`/`summary` of failed actions are never redacted (characterization test). | `src/lib/actions/core.ts:685` (`audit`), `:725` (`redact`) | `audit-secret-leakage.test.ts` (`it.fails`), `redaction-coverage.test.ts` |

## 8. Decisions and assumptions already made (do not undo)

- `it.fails` + finding id in the name is the convention for real vulnerabilities; the failing reason is guarded by a CONTROL test where ambiguity was possible (e.g. SEC-F5 has a "harness works" test that proves tofu evaluates `${upper("abc")}`; SEC-F1 has a characterization test). Flip to `it` when the owning code is fixed.
- Redaction coverage is a **ratchet** (exact map), measured with `stable` canaries (value depends only on label+shape) because whether a random 40-char key contains `/` decides whether a URL regex catches it; AWS secret keys are excluded from URL-userinfo positions for that reason.
- `canarySecret` default seed is constant (reproducible runs), not random.
- v2 matrix uses an in-memory SQLite journal injected through `globalThis.__zenithAgentJournal` (the file journal refuses Windows) and env `ZENITH_AGENT_CONTROL=1`, `ZENITH_AGENT_WRITES=1`, loopback origin.
- v1/v2 "target-workspace" naming mode sets `noExistenceLeak:false` because the call is refused at the workspace check regardless of existence (comparing it with a phantom compares different refusal levels). `poison` principal is exempt from the existence comparison (its grant itself lists the foreign id).
- `zenith_get_manifest` view=working ignores `environmentId` (not a leak; the project is its target); noted in the test.
- The policy tests build their own `PolicyInput` (`tests/_support/security/policy.ts`) instead of importing `tests/policy/support.ts`.
- Windows tooling gotchas (cost me hours): the Bash tool rewrites `\uXXXX` sequences and backslash pairs typed in commands/heredocs into real characters, and Python `open(p,'w')` rewrites LF as CRLF. Edit files with the Write/Edit tools, or Python with `newline=''`; the repo is LF (`.gitattributes eol=lf`). Never put `\u` escapes in a shell command. After scripted edits run `grep -c $'\r'` / check for raw invisible characters; I already converted raw invisible characters in test sources back to `\uXXXX` escapes.
- No file outside the owned paths was modified. `git status` after the merge is clean apart from my commits. The merge of `platform/integration` was explicitly permitted by the coordinator (message of 2026-10-01); an earlier misrouted coordinator message addressed to WS-INC was ignored as instructed.
- Honest unknowns: I did NOT read the merged credential broker, workflows, observability, incidents, reconcile or analysis implementations; every statement about them in the threat model must be verified against code before it is written as a control. ## 9. Raw material for THREAT-MODEL.md

Evidence legend to use: **E** = exists (path), **W** = written by WS-SEC (path), **P** = pending (workstream + what to write). "Control" must cite a file/function.

### Assets (table: asset, where it lives, impact of loss, controls, status)
OIDC signing key (RS256, `ZENITH_OIDC_SIGNING_JWK`, KMS in production, ADR-0006; `src/lib/credentials/signing`, public JWKS routes exist); control signing key (Ed25519, `ZENITH_CONTROL_SIGNING_JWK`, signs job envelopes/machine requests/capability grants, RUNNER-PROTOCOL.md section 1); platform DB (schema `platform`, `src/lib/controlplane/db`, Postgres/PGlite, ADR-0002; no RLS found, tenant scoping is in SQL + the sweep + `controlplane-sql-scoping.test.ts`); customer cloud roles (observe/deploy, ExternalId or OIDC `sub`, session policies; `credentials/types.ts`, `bootstrap-templates.test.ts`); runner identity keys (Ed25519, per agent, never leaves host; control-plane side `repos/runners.ts` + nonces); approvals (`repos/approvals.ts`, `controlplane/approvals`; and the legacy v2 journal `control/journal.ts review/claim`); plan files (binary tofu plan, embeds unmasked values, server-side only, `engine.ts planFileSha`, mode 0600); vault key (`ZENITH_SECRET_KEY`, AES-256-GCM `src/lib/secrets/index.ts`, single key, no KMS, `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`); plus: agent credentials `za_` (hashed at rest, <=30 d), Temporal history, policy bundle (`policy/dist/{policy.wasm,manifest.json}`), audit log, repository content/manifest, customer state bucket, `ZENITH_BACKUP_KEY`.

### Trust boundaries (table: boundary, what crosses, authn, key controls, status)
browser (session cookie + verified email; approvals only via `browser()` in `control/browser.ts`, refuses any request with an Authorization header, origin/CSRF check); model/agent (Navigator + connected coding agents: propose only, invariant 1/9; `za_` scoped credential); MCP bearer (`za_` + OAuth resource-server mode `control/oauth.ts`); control plane (capability broker WS-CAP planned, REST `/api/platform/v1` planned); execution worker (Temporal activities; WS-WF merged; credentials only in `withSession`); Temporal history (ids+digests only, ADR-0009; test pending); runner (outbound-only, signed requests/jobs, RUNNER-PROTOCOL.md; Go WS-GO, server side WS-RUNSRV); zenithd (fixed-code operations, local guards, JSONL audit); customer cloud (STS/WIF, session policy, permission boundary, state in customer S3); repository content (untrusted data; importers, analysis, hosted source intake `src/lib/hosted/source/{tar,validate}.ts`); logs (untrusted; observability `escape.ts`/`redact.ts`, reader excludes logs by default).

### STRIDE per component (condense into one table)
Cover: web/API, MCP v1/v2, capability broker (planned), policy engine, approval service, operations store/leases, execution worker + Temporal, credential broker, tofu runner, runner/zenithd, observability, incident engine, analysis. S/T/R/I/D/E each with control + evidence.

### Threat register: starting content per threat (verify before writing)
1. **Malicious repository**: importers produce closed-vocabulary manifests, terraform importer only yields `referenced` resources (`importers/terraform.ts`); analysis hardened vs hostile compose/terraform (commit `2c4781c`, `tests/analysis/hostile.test.ts` E); hosted source intake rejects traversal/symlinks/zip bombs (`hosted/source/tar.ts`, hosted threat model section 2); builds in customer CodeBuild (ADR-0016, planned WS-AWS-CMP); assembler (W). Residual: builds still execute hostile code; esbuild parsing; SEC-F5.
2. **Prompt injection in repo files**: invariant 9; MCP initialize `instructions` tell the model to treat repo text as data (`agent-access/http.ts`, `control/http.ts`); `planView.untrustedValues:true` + control-char stripping (W `tofu-secrets.test.ts`); `incidents/sanitize.ts` + `tests/incidents/hostile.test.ts` (E); observability `escape.ts` (E); approvals human-only digest-bound; policy `agent_high_risk_requires_approval`. Residual: SEC-F7 invisible Unicode; SEC-F8; models can still be persuaded to PROPOSE bad changes (approval is the control).
3. **Malicious log content**: observability escape/redact (E), reader excludes log events from `zenith_get_events` and gates `zenith_get_logs` behind `logs` scope + redaction + warning (W `mcp-secret-leakage.test.ts`), log forging corpus. Residual: free-text secrets survive redaction (ratchet).
4. **Malicious tofu output**: `parseShowJson`/`normalizePlan` fail closed (format version, tofu version, errored, unknown actions) (E `tests/tofu/plan.test.ts`), output values dropped when sensitive, `renderUiStream`, byte caps (64 MiB show, 8 MiB output), `planView` bounds. Residual: LIMITS pinned in `tofu-secrets.test.ts`.
5. **Compromised agent**: `za_` credential = one workspace, chosen projects/environments, ticked scopes, <=30 d, revocable, nothing cached; approvals browser-only; v2 prepare/execute split with digest-bound human review, fingerprint recheck, `uncertain` on ambiguity (E `tests/agent-control-*.test.ts`); policy origin rules; W: `agent-credentials`, v1/v2 matrices, `policy-invariants` P7. Residual: SEC-F8; a human can approve their own agent's proposal (no separation unless policy `twoPersonProduction`); device-flow code phishing (`link/protocol.ts`, `control/browser.ts browserLinkApprove`; client name is shown as "unverified").
6. **Compromised coding connector**: same blast radius as 5 plus OAuth mode (`control/oauth.ts`: issuer, audience=resource, alg allowlist, required claims, <=1 h lifetime, `bindGrant` requires a browser-created grant); plugin supply chain lives in a separate repo (`GODOSTROYER/Zenith-plugins`, branch `hardening/plugin-provenance`, see production-hardening docs). Residual: connector sees everything the credential can read (redaction gaps).
7. **Cloud credential theft**: no long-lived customer secrets stored (ADR-0006); creds only inside `withSession` (`credentials/index.ts` - verify); tofu child env allowlist (W `tofu-runner-env.test.ts`); output redaction by exact value + patterns. Residual: the tofu child holds live creds in its environment, so SEC-F5 (file read of `/proc/self/environ`) is the path to steal them; session env is a denylist (SEC-F6); IMDS reachability on the worker host.
8. **Confused deputy**: ExternalId per connection (`credentials/types.ts AwsConnectionConfig.externalId`), OIDC `sub zenith:ws:<ws>:conn:<conn>` pinned by the customer's trust policy, grant workspace must equal connection workspace (`credentials/grants.ts` - verify), session tags, bootstrap templates (`tests/credentials/bootstrap-templates.test.ts` E). Pending W: item 2a.
9. **Cross-tenant access**: W v1/v2 matrices; E `tests/actions/workspace-isolation.test.ts`, `tests/controlplane/tenancy.test.ts`, W `controlplane-sql-scoping.test.ts`; SEC-F1. Residual: product store (PostgREST snapshots) tenancy is app-level, no RLS.
10. **SSRF**: `alerts/webhook-policy.ts` (https only, no userinfo/fragment, ports 443/8443, every resolved address checked, address pinned for connect, redirects refused in `deliver.ts:351`) E `tests/alerts/webhook-policy.test.ts` + W `ssrf-address-oracle.test.ts`; runner probes refuse metadata/link-local (RUNNER-PROTOCOL.md section 4; Go tests - cite `go/`); observability source URLs (verify, see 2c); hosted gateway. Residual: DNS rebinding handled by pinning only on the webhook path.
11. **Metadata-service access**: webhook policy blocks 169.254.169.254, 100.100.100.200, fd00:ec2::254, GCP/Azure names (relaxation env cannot unblock metadata); runner refuses; tofu child on an EC2/ECS worker can still reach IMDS through the AWS provider chain unless the worker enforces IMDSv2 hop limit 1 (deployment requirement, planned WS-CI/WS-DOCS).
12. **Webhook abuse**: same module + 64 KiB response cap, HMAC signature with per-channel secret (vault), pinned delivery; E `tests/alerts/delivery.test.ts`. Residual: operator-supplied URLs are an SSRF primitive by nature.
13. **Arbitrary code execution (builds)**: ADR-0016; hosted recipe runners honestly labelled (`docs/hosted/THREAT-MODEL.md` section 2); `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in Dockerfile/CI; provisioners/connection/remote-state blocked by the assembler; tofu not sandboxed beyond env allowlist and process-tree kill (`runner.ts` header). Residual: SEC-F5.
14. **Supply-chain compromise**: lockfile + `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (Dockerfile:27, ci.yml), exact provider pins with multi-platform hash lockfiles and `-lockfile=readonly` (`tofu/providers.ts`, `locks/`, E `tests/tofu/providers.test.ts`), OPA bundle rebuilt in CI and sha256-recorded in decisions, CI supply-chain gate and dependabot (WS-CI merged; read `.github/workflows`), Go modules (check `go.sum`/vuln scan). Residual: `checkTofuVersion` checks the version string, not a checksum of the binary (worker image must verify the download); registry-level compromise of a pinned version is caught only by hashes.
15. **Runner compromise**: per-request Ed25519 signatures, nonce replay cache, 60 s skew, revoked => stop; job JWS bound to runner id + grant + expiry + nonce; kind allowlists; SigV4 proxy action allowlist; first-writer-wins results; registration token single-use (E `repos/runners.ts`, `tests/controlplane/runners.test.ts`; server transport planned WS-RUNSRV; Go WS-GO). Residual: a compromised runner holds the customer's local identity (by design) and can lie about results (uncertain, reconcile).
16. **zenithd compromise**: fixed-code operations, argv only, unit-name regex, local allowlists, `exec.enabled:false` default, JSONL audit; control-plane side planned WS-MACH. Residual: root on the VM.
17. **TOCTOU plan->apply**: plan digest binds configDigest+lockDigest+tofuVersion+changes; sensitive changes bound via HMAC fingerprint; `applyVerifiedPlan` re-plans and refuses on a moved digest, applies the plan file it just verified, refuses a plan file that changed while verifying (E `tests/tofu/runner.test.ts`, W rotation test in `tofu-secrets.test.ts`); v2 journal fingerprint recheck (`stale_plan`) and approval digest; grants bind op+digest. Residual: window between `show` and `apply`; cloud drift is handled by tofu's own plan staleness.
18. **Approval replay**: v2: `review` requires phase prepared + exact digest, expiry <=15 min, `claim` is one atomic transition (E `tests/agent-control-journal*.test.ts`); platform: approvals consumed in the claiming transaction (`repos/approvals.ts consume`, E `tests/controlplane/approvals.test.ts`), grants single-use by `jti` (`repos/grants.ts`).
19. **Stale authorization**: `Coordinator.execute` re-authenticates before and after dispatch, rechecks `authorize`, fingerprint, application authority digest; revocation effective on the next request; policy version re-evaluated at execution; ends `uncertain` instead of success (E `tests/agent-control-coordinator.test.ts`).
20. **Operation duplication**: workflow id `op-<operationId>` (ADR-0009), durable idempotency keyed by workspace+principal+capability bound to input digest (`repos/idempotency.ts`), v2 unique (workspace, subject, requestKey) + intent hash, env leases with fence tokens (`repos/leases.ts`), `uncertain` is never auto-retried (E `tests/controlplane/{operations,leases}.test.ts`, `tests/workflows/failures.test.ts`). Residual: legacy `core.ts` idempotency is process-local (documented in its header).
21. **Cloud eventual consistency**: "unknown is a value" (invariant 7), observations/runtime separate from desired, verify checks with `passed:"unknown"`, reconciliation (WS-REC merged), `uncertain`. Residual: verify steps for real AWS are not exercised without credentials (B-AWS-LIVE).
22. **DNS takeover (dangling records)**: policy `dnsChanges` fact => admin approval in production (`production_network_identity_change`); detection of dangling records on deprovision is NOT implemented as far as I read (verify `src/lib/reconcile`, drivers WS-AWS-NET); mark planned.
23. **Destructive data action**: policy `production_destroys_data`, `production_database_delete`, `production_destructive_requires_admin`; `DEFAULT_STATEFUL_TYPES`; plan facts `destroysData`; legacy engine stateful-deletion block (E `tests/actions/stateful-deletion.test.ts`); W `policy-invariants` P2/P6. Residual: policy only sees what plan facts extract; backup existence is not checked.
24. **Dependency confusion**: provider sources are fully qualified (`registry.opentofu.org/hashicorp/aws`, `oracle/oci`) and hash-locked; check for an `.npmrc`/scopes and Go module paths (verify); no private package names observed. Mark unverified where not read.
25. **Secret leakage via plan/logs/events/MCP**: primary control = values never enter records (refs only); W ratchets: `tofu-secrets`, `mcp-secret-leakage`, `redaction-coverage`, `audit-secret-leakage`; SEC-R1; events/evidence repos have no scrubbing (item 2d).
26. **Temporal history exposure**: payloads ids+digests only (ADR-0009); pending W test (item 2b); Temporal Cloud/self-hosted trust and payload codec to be stated honestly.
27. **Policy bundle tampering**: load fails closed on wasm/manifest mismatch, truncation, bad entrypoint, non-wasm (W `policy-invariants` P9, E `tests/policy/engine.test.ts`); decision records store bundle sha256; CI rebuild diff gate. Residual (pinned characterization): no pinned expected hash; a writer of `policy/dist` can rewrite the manifest too.
28. (extra row) **Runtime/engine defects**: SEC-F9.
